title.narrative: Lifesaving Protection, WASH, NFIs, Health and Nutrition Assistance to Displacement and Famine in South Kordofan and North Kordofan

description.narrative: ltpgtHumanitarian needs in the states of North Kordofan and South Kordofan are critically high due to ongoing conflict and limited access to humanitarian aid, with particularly high needs identified in the localities of Kadugli (SK), Dilling (SK), and Sheikan (NK). Vulnerable children and families face barriers to accessing healthcare, shelter and basic services due to the disruption of supplies, infrastructure damage, displacements, and imposed restrictions. As part of its ongoing humanitarian response program in the Kordofan region, SC and partners Plan and CDF, propose a seven-month project that aims to reduce morbidity and mortality and to improve the living conditions and safety of displaced individuals and host communities in Kadugli, Dilling, and Sheikan. In line with the HRP and cluster objectives, the project will deliver safe, timely, principled and gender-responsive assistance to ltbgt106,847 peoplelt/bgt and target the most vulnerable population groups such as women, men, children and persons with disabilities. ltbrgtUnder the leadership of SC, the Consortium will contribute to improving equitable and inclusive access to quality life-saving curative and preventative healthcare services to 20,4000 people (16,540 specifically for nutrition) through seven health facilities in Dilling (3), Sheikan (2) and Kadugli (2). To fill identified health and nutrition gaps including medical supplies, incentives, minor rehabilitation and referrals and increase the coverage, the project will target women of reproductive age, with a focus on pregnant and lactating women, and children under 5 years of age, while providing gender-sensitive and disability-inclusive lifesaving healthcare for communicable and non-communicable diseases among children over 5, adults and the elderly. The proposed health interventions will provide essential maternal and child health services, essential medication, and supplies (PPE, diagnostics, case management), establish referral pathways and strengthen the immunization services. SC will also provide emergency lifesaving nutrition services with an emphasis on increasing access for conflict-affected people in all targeted localities, including community management of acute malnutrition (CMAM) and preventive nutrition services. The project will be securing nutrition supplies, contributing to facilities running cost, and establishing linkages between stabilisation centres, OTP and TSFP sites. Likewise, the Consortium will ensure that targeted health facilities are equipped with necessary WASH infrastructure and materials, including water purification systems, excreta disposal facilities, cleaning materials, and solid waste management systems. We will also ensure that targeted communities have access to safe WASH services including access to safe water, sanitation, proper waste management and hygiene promotion.ltbrgtUnder the Shelter/NFI component, Plan International will provide NFI and shelter to support essential daily activities and offer adaptable shelter solutions to 16,900 people. This will include life-saving in-kind non-food items to the most vulnerable IDPs and host communities, distribute cash for shelter/NFIs to assist affected households to establish or rehabilitate shelters, supply and construct emergency shelter with high-standards and provide materials for the construction of emergency shelter.ltbrgtLastly, under the leadership of CDF, the Consortium will provide an integrated GBV, CP and GP response to conflict-affected communities in Dilling locality. CDF will Establish of two child protection networks and strengthen prevention activities of Community Engagement, provide specialized services through case management, run and operate CFS/ WGSS, conduct GBV/CP awareness raising campaign, case management, provide support and assistance to SGBV survivors, among others. ltbrgt ltbrgtlt/pgt
